item.title: Article: Anthropic goes public... to stay private.
item.description: What Anthropic's final prospectus and the court record show on its first day of trading: who holds the votes, who holds the contracts and where the government's leverage sits. No government stake or seat, and listing makes the national-lab comparison less convincing.

item.title: Podcast: Frontier labs as national laboratories, the October newsletter
item.description: Frontier AI labs already get lab-style treatment from the US government, but through one-off levers rather than the contract that makes national labs open, graded and replaceable. This episode walks through the October issue of the Frontier Labs newsletter on xanderpico.com: the six levers in use, estimates for nine paths to 2030, the strongest objection, and what to watch next. Every claim comes from the published newsletter, which lists all 37 sources. The hosts, George and Jessica, are AI voices.

item.title: Thread: Frontier labs as national laboratories
item.description: As national security and international competition press on the frontier AI labs, which past model of a national laboratory do they come to resemble, and where does the comparison break down? An essay on whether national security, secure methods and international competition will push the frontier AI labs toward national-laboratory status, and what past labs suggest about the shape that could take.

item.title: Newsletter: Frontier AI labs are already treated like national labs. Just not the way that counts.
item.description: The short written issue behind the paths tracker: what the US government does to frontier AI labs now, why it is not the national-lab contract, and where it probably goes by 2030. Read online.
